title: US Regulators Approve ‘Net Neutrality’ for Internet Providers

image.attribution: Dr. Avishai Teicher Pikiwiki Israel / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-2.5

main_content:
U.S. regulators have approved rules banning so-called paid prioritization, in which big Internet service providers would charge content providers a higher fee to stream their material over cyberspace faster than smaller customers.

In a 3-2 vote along party lines, with Democrats in support, the Federal Communications Commission’s approved new “net neutrality” rules capping a year of intense debate between supporters of online companies such as Google and Netflix, as well as those of major service providers such as AT&T and Comcast.

The rules ban Internet providers from blocking and unfairly slowing down any web traffic on their pipes or striking deals with content companies for faster or smoother downloads, among other things. Republicans argue the broad scope of the rules represents government overreach.

questions.question: What do the new FCC rules aim to establish regarding internet service?
options: A fair and open internet for all users
Increased revenue for major internet providers
More power for content creators over providers
Removal of all regulations on internet service
questions.answer: A fair and open internet for all users

questions.question: What does 'paid prioritization' mean?
options: Charging content providers for faster streaming of their materials
Offering free access to all websites regardless of speed
Limiting internet access to small companies only
Creating a tiered system for basic internet services
questions.answer: Charging content providers for faster streaming of their materials

questions.question: What are the FCC's new rules intended to prevent?
options: Blocking and unfairly slowing down web traffic
Increasing internet speed for all users
Reducing government regulation of the internet
Encouraging deals between internet providers and content companies
questions.answer: Blocking and unfairly slowing down web traffic
